whyWrong.du: After aimer, liking something in general takes the definite le — j'aime le café.
whyWrong.de: de alone doesn't fit — general likes take le café.
whyWrong.un: un café is 'a coffee' (one cup) — liking coffee in general is le café.

whyWrong.de la: After adorer, general likes take the definite la, not partitive de la.
whyWrong.une: une is 'a' — loving music in general uses la musique.
whyWrong.le: musique is feminine — la musique, not le.

whyWrong.des: Liking cats in general takes the definite les, not des.
whyWrong.de: de doesn't fit — general likes take les chats.
whyWrong.le: chats is plural — les chats, not le.

items.sentenceTrans: I like dancing with my friends.

whyWrong.danse: After aimer you need the infinitive danser, not danse.
whyWrong.à danser: aimer takes the infinitive directly — no à: j'aime danser.
whyWrong.que je danse: aimer + infinitive here — not a 'que' clause.

whyWrong.de: aimer keeps the definite le even in the negative — pas le café.
whyWrong.du: Liking/disliking in general takes le, not partitive du.
whyWrong.d': d' is de before a vowel, and aimer keeps le anyway.

items.fullSentence: Je préfère le cinéma au théâtre.

whyWrong.à le: à + le contracts to au — au théâtre, never 'à le'.
whyWrong.à la: théâtre is masculine — à + le = au, not à la.
whyWrong.que le: préférer X à Y uses à for 'to', not que.

items.sentenceTrans: I hate cooking in the evening.

whyWrong.cuisine: Conjugated form — after détester use the infinitive: cuisiner.
whyWrong.cuisines: Conjugated (tu) form — use the infinitive: cuisiner.
whyWrong.à cuisiner: No à after détester — the infinitive follows directly.

items.fullSentence: J'adore la musique — c'est ma passion !
items.sentenceTrans: I LOVE music — it's my passion!

whyWrong.aime: j'aime is only 'I like' — 'ma passion' calls for the stronger j'adore.
whyWrong.aime pas: Negative (and missing ne) — the sentence is enthusiastic.
